365Scores: 365Scores runs a popular free mobile and web app that delivers real-time sports scores, stats, news and personalized alerts across football and many other sports and competitions worldwide. It makes money through a freemium model driven mainly by in-app advertising, plus premium subscriptions and affiliate/betting referral revenue. Founded in Tel Aviv in 2012, it was acquired by UK gambling group Entain in 2023 for roughly $160 million.
Blockaid: Blockaid is a Web3/onchain security company (Tel Aviv and New York) whose engine simulates and scans blockchain transactions in real time to block scams, phishing, malicious dApps and hacks before a user signs. It sells this protection as a B2B SaaS/API service to crypto wallets and platforms, earning subscription/usage fees; customers include MetaMask, OpenSea, Coinbase and other major wallets and exchanges. Founded in 2022 by ex-Israeli cyber-intelligence veterans, it is venture-backed with roughly $83 million+ raised from investors like Ribbit, Sequoia and Greylock.
Bounce AI: Bounce is a Tel Aviv-based fintech that offers an AI-powered debt collection and resolution platform, giving borrowers a self-service portal to view balances and set up flexible payment plans while helping creditors recover debt more efficiently. It is a B2B business that earns SaaS/service fees from the lenders that use its platform, and says it is used by 50+ banks, fintechs and credit unions. It is a venture-backed private startup (seed-stage funding from investors including Pagaya, Nyca Partners and Harel), with roughly 50-200 employees.
Cato Networks: Cato Networks provides a cloud-native SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) platform that combines enterprise networking (SD-WAN) and security into a single global service delivered from the cloud. It makes money through recurring subscriptions, and reported surpassing $350 million in annual recurring revenue in 2025 with 40%+ year-over-year growth. It remains a private company, valued at more than $4.8 billion after a 2025 funding round, serving 3,000+ enterprises.
CommIT: CommIT (formerly Comm-IT) is an Israeli technology group that provides software engineering and IT services, embedding expert development teams and building custom software and products for startups and enterprises. It earns revenue primarily by billing for professional/engineering services and consulting (project- and team-based contracts), alongside its product offerings. It is a privately held company with over 1,000 employees and offices across Israel, the US, Canada, the UK and Europe.
DealHub: DealHub is a SaaS company (Tel Aviv and Austin) offering an AI-powered 'quote-to-revenue' platform, including CPQ (Configure-Price-Quote), contract lifecycle management, DealRoom, subscription management and billing that plug into CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot. It makes money through recurring software subscription fees based on the modules and seats customers buy. It is privately held, reached roughly $60 million+ in revenue in 2024, and has raised about $184 million including a $100 million growth round in early 2026; customers include Intuit, Gong and Braze.
Fiverr: Fiverr operates an online marketplace that connects businesses with freelancers offering digital services such as design, writing, marketing and software work. It makes money primarily by taking a transaction fee/commission on each order (service fees charged to both buyers and sellers), supplemented by subscriptions, promoted listings and other seller tools. Fiverr is a publicly traded company listed on the NYSE (ticker FVRR).
Global-e: Global-e provides an end-to-end platform that lets retailers and brands sell direct-to-consumer across borders, handling localized checkout, currencies, duties/taxes, shipping and compliance. It makes money by charging merchants fees tied to the gross merchandise value (GMV) and transactions processed through its platform, plus fulfillment/service revenue. It is publicly traded on Nasdaq (GLBE), reported roughly $750 million in revenue for 2024, and has a notable strategic partnership with Shopify.
Guardio: Guardio is a Tel Aviv-based consumer cybersecurity company best known for a browser extension (and mobile app) that protects everyday users against phishing, scam sites, malicious extensions and identity theft. It makes money through paid subscriptions (roughly $10-13/month plans covering multiple family members), with nearly all revenue coming from individual consumers. It is a fast-growing private company that raised an $80 million Series B in 2025 and expected to surpass $100 million in ARR by early 2026.
Holisto: Holisto (formerly Splitty) is an Israeli travel-tech company that runs a hotel-booking platform using a price-aggregation and 'deal assembly' engine to combine rates and coupons into cheaper hotel bookings for consumers. As a direct-to-consumer online booking site, it earns revenue mainly through commissions/margins on the hotel bookings it facilitates. Founded in 2015, it was fully acquired by travel giant Trivago in 2025 (for about $25 million) and continues to operate with a team of around 250 people.
Playtika: Playtika is a developer and publisher of free-to-play mobile and social games (including casino-style and casual titles like Slotomania, Bingo Blitz and June's Journey). It makes money overwhelmingly through in-app purchases of virtual items (around 98% of revenue), with a growing but smaller share from in-game advertising, relying on data-driven live operations to monetize a large player base. It is publicly traded on Nasdaq (PLTK) and generates roughly $2.5 billion in annual revenue.
Port: Port (getport.io) is an Israeli software company whose product is an Internal Developer Portal (IDP) - a centralized platform that gives engineering teams a single interface to catalog their software, services, and infrastructure and self-serve DevOps actions, increasingly positioned as a hub for agentic AI workflows. It makes money as B2B SaaS, charging enterprises subscription fees for the platform. Founded in 2022, it is a venture-backed private company that raised a $35M Series B in 2024 and reportedly a $100M round in late 2025; customers include GitHub, LG, and BT.
Rapyd: Rapyd is an Israeli-founded (London-headquartered) fintech-as-a-service company offering a global 'payments in a box' platform - digital wallets, card issuing, fund disbursement, fraud protection, and local + cross-border payments across 100+ countries - accessible via API. It makes money primarily through transaction and processing fees on the payments flowing through its network, plus fees for related financial services. It is a private company that was once Israel's most valuable startup (~$10B valuation in 2021), though its valuation has since fallen sharply (reportedly sought funding around $3.5B in 2025).
Similarweb: Similarweb is an Israeli digital-intelligence company that aggregates web and app traffic data to give businesses analytics on website/app performance, competitor benchmarking, market research, SEO, and audience insights. It makes money mainly through tiered SaaS subscriptions, supplemented by API/data access and custom research. It is publicly traded on the NYSE (ticker SMWB), reached positive operating profit for the first time in 2026, and generates roughly $75M+ in quarterly revenue with a growing enterprise customer base.
Sunflower: Sunflower is an early-stage Israeli B2C gaming startup based in Tel Aviv operating in the social/casual gaming space (its social-gaming products include live-style games such as poker, roulette, and slots). Like most B2C social gaming companies, it would monetize primarily through in-app purchases of virtual currency/items and related consumer spending rather than subscriptions. It is a small, private, venture-backed company; detailed public information on scale and funding is limited, so specifics beyond this are uncertain.
Taboola: Taboola is an Israeli content-recommendation and advertising company that powers the 'sponsored content' / recommendation widgets on publisher websites, connecting advertisers with audiences across a large network of premium publishers. It makes money as a two-sided ad marketplace, primarily via cost-per-click advertising (over 90% of revenue), paying publishers a share of revenue (traffic acquisition cost) and keeping the rest. It is publicly traded on Nasdaq (ticker TBLA, via a 2021 SPAC) with revenue of roughly $450M+ per quarter, and is shifting toward performance advertising.
Tavily: Tavily is an Israeli/US AI company that provides a web-search API purpose-built for LLMs and AI agents, letting applications fetch and retrieve real-time, structured web data through a single API call (it grew out of the open-source GPT Researcher project). It makes money via a usage-based API model (developers pay per search/request, with paid tiers above a free allowance). Founded in 2023, it raised ~$25M (including a $20M Series A led by Insight Partners in 2025), serves 2M+ developers, and in early 2026 was acquired by Nebius Group for around $275M (up to ~$400M with milestones).
Team8: Team8 is an Israeli company-building 'foundry' and venture capital group that co-founds and builds startups from scratch (alongside making VC investments), focused on cybersecurity, data & AI, fintech, and digital health. It makes money like a VC/foundry - through equity ownership and returns in the companies it creates and backs, funded by capital from its own investment funds/LPs. Founded in 2014 by former leaders of Israel's Unit 8200 (including Nadav Zafrir), it is backed by corporations such as Microsoft, Walmart, Cisco, Barclays, and Moody's, and has spun out numerous notable security startups.
WalkMe: WalkMe is a Tel Aviv-based pioneer of the Digital Adoption Platform (DAP) - software that overlays on top of other applications to provide in-app guidance, walkthroughs, tips, and automation so employees and users can navigate enterprise software more effectively. It makes money through B2B SaaS subscriptions to enterprises. Formerly public on Nasdaq (WKME), it was acquired by SAP for about $1.5 billion in 2024; it has 2,000+ customers including IBM and Nestle.
Wix: Wix is an Israeli cloud-based website-building platform that lets individuals and businesses create and manage websites and online stores with no coding, plus related tools (e-commerce, bookings, payments). It operates on a freemium model and makes money mainly through premium subscriptions (its Creative Subscriptions segment) and Business Solutions such as domains, professional email, payment processing, and app-store services; only a small percentage of its 250M+ registered users convert to paying, but average revenue per user grows over time. It is publicly traded on Nasdaq (ticker WIX) with over $1.7B in annual revenue.
Yotpo: Yotpo is an Israeli e-commerce marketing platform that gives online brands an integrated suite of tools - customer reviews and ratings, SMS and email marketing, loyalty and referral programs, and subscriptions - often integrated with Shopify. It makes money through SaaS subscriptions to its marketing modules (with pricing scaling by usage/tier). It is a private, venture-backed company that raised a $230M Series F in 2021 at a ~$2.5B valuation (investors include Bessemer and Shopify) and serves 30,000+ brands including Patagonia and Steve Madden.
Abra: Abra (abra-it / abra-rnd) is a large Israeli technology services and solutions group of 1,000+ experts that designs, builds, and integrates enterprise systems across BI & AI, ERP, CRM, cybersecurity, cloud & infrastructure, custom software R&D, and e-commerce for organizations. It makes money primarily as an IT services / systems-integration and consulting business - project-based development, integration, and managed services, plus reselling/implementing partner platforms. It is a partner of major vendors such as Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP, Oracle, and AWS; it is an established Israeli IT group rather than a single-product startup (not to be confused with the Abra crypto wallet).
